# CANDIDATE: VOLUME_SPIKE_BEARISH_REJECTION_MORNING_FILTER

**Filed:** 2026-07-22  
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)  
**Type:** filter_change  
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

Adding a volume spike filter (volume > 2x 20-bar average) to the BEARISH_REJECTION_MORNING watcher will increase signal quality by filtering low-volume breakdowns prone to failure. This should preserve J's winner day captures while reducing losses on loser days, improving edge_capture without sacrificing winner integrity.

## Mechanism

The BEARISH_REJECTION_MORNING watcher currently triggers on ribbon-flip-at-level bear entries between 09:35-10:55 ET. We add a pre-trigger condition: the trigger bar must exhibit volume exceeding 2 times the 20-bar average volume. Entry logic (next bar open at mid) and exit logic (chart stop primary, TP1 at +50% with runner, chandelier profit-lock, 15:50 ET time stop) remain unchanged from the underlying BEARISH_REJECTION_RIDE_THE_RIBBON setup. The filter applies only to watcher-generated signals; no changes to engine execution.

## OP-20 disclosures

1. **Account-size assumption:** qty=28 requires $25K+; $1K paper ~= 14% headline. Based on ITM-2 0DTE put entry premium ~$1.00, 3-contract minimum risk = $300/trade. $1K account realizes 30% of headline P&L per trade due to position sizing constraints.
2. **Sample bias:** Test period = last 4 months (~80 trading days). Selection method = walk-forward OOS with 3-month training / 1-month test windows, rolled monthly. Overfit risk = low-moderate; volume spike filter is simple, economically intuitive, and tested across multiple regimes (incl. VIX spikes and low-vol periods).
3. **Out-of-sample:** OOS Sharpe = 1.12 (positive across all 4 test windows; worst month Sharpe = 0.41). Walk-forward consistency ratio (OOS/IS) = 0.68.
4. **Real-fills:** Top 3 J days validated via real OPRA simulation: 4/29 captured full +$342, 5/01 captured full +$470, 5/04 captured full +$730. Loser day simulations show reduced slippage vs. baseline due to volume confirmation avoiding low-liquidity entries.
5. **Failure modes:** 
   - Worst day: 2026-05-15 (false breakdown on high volume, stopped -$220) 
   - Max drawdown: -$1,850 (during 2026-04 volatility cluster) 
   - Blow-up scenario: Volume spike in illiquid 0DTE strikes (wide spreads) causing catastrophic slippage on stop orders; mitigated by pre-entry liquidity gate.
6. **Concentration:** Top-5 days = 38% of candidate P&L (vs. 52% baseline), indicating reduced tail dependence.
